description: Prepositions establish relationships between a noun or pronoun and other words in a sentence. Conjunctions connect words, phrases, or clauses to build logical sentence structures.

sections.title: Basic Concepts of Prepositions
sections.description: Correct usage of prepositions indicating time, place, and direction.

key_concepts.explanation: Use 'at' for a specific time, 'on' for days and dates, and 'in' for months, years, or long periods.
Use 'at' for a specific point or location, 'on' for a surface, and 'in' for an enclosed space.

examples.incorrect_or_context: I will meet you in Monday at 2024.
examples.correct_or_usage: I will meet you on Monday in 2024.
examples.explanation: 'Monday' is a day, so 'on' is required. '2024' is a year, which takes 'in'.

exceptions.explanation: Prepositions like 'in', 'on', or 'at' are omitted before words such as today, tomorrow, yesterday, next, and last.
exceptions.example: He will come on tomorrow (Incorrect) -> He will come tomorrow (Correct).

sections.title: Confusing & Fixed Prepositions
sections.description: Distinguishing between prepositions with similar meanings and mastering fixed preposition combinations.

grammar_rules.explanation: Certain words are always followed by a specific preposition, regardless of direct translation logic. Examples: 'Fond of', 'Accused of', 'Rely on'.

key_concepts.explanation: 'Between' is used when referring to two persons or things, whereas 'Among' is used for more than two.
'In' indicates a state of rest or position inside something, while 'Into' indicates motion or direction towards the inside.

examples.explanation: Jumping involves motion, so 'into' must be used instead of 'in'.

examples.incorrect_or_context: She is fond for classical music.
examples.correct_or_usage: She is fond of classical music.
examples.explanation: The word 'fond' always takes the fixed preposition 'of'.

sections.title: Types and Rules of Conjunctions
sections.description: Understanding various types of conjunctions and their grammatical constraints.

grammar_rules.structure: Noun + Conjunction + Noun / Verb + Conjunction + Verb
grammar_rules.explanation: Coordinating Conjunctions (FANBOYS: For, And, Nor, But, Or, Yet, So) must always connect elements of equal grammatical rank (e.g., a gerund to a gerund, an adjective to an adjective).

key_concepts.explanation: These conjunctions connect a dependent clause to an independent (main) clause to establish a relationship like cause, condition, or contrast. Examples: Because, Although, If, Unless.

examples.incorrect_or_context: He likes reading and to write.
examples.explanation: 'And' must connect parallel structures. Since 'reading' is a gerund, 'to write' (infinitive) must be changed to 'writing' (gerund).

exceptions.explanation: The conjunction 'but' is never used with 'Although' or 'Though'. Instead, use a comma or the word 'yet'.
exceptions.example: Although he is rich, but he is sad (Incorrect) -> Although he is rich, yet he is sad (Correct).

sections.title: Correlative Conjunctions
sections.description: Rules for conjunctions used in pairs and maintaining sentence parallelism.

grammar_rules.structure: Either Sub1 + or Sub2 + Verb (according to Sub2)
grammar_rules.explanation: When two subjects are joined by Either...or, Neither...nor, or Not only...but also, the verb must agree with the subject closest to it.

examples.incorrect_or_context: Neither the manager nor the employees was present.
examples.correct_or_usage: Neither the manager nor the employees were present.
examples.explanation: The verb is closest to the plural subject 'employees', so the plural verb 'were' is required.

examples.incorrect_or_context: He not only speaks English but also French.
examples.correct_or_usage: He speaks not only English but also French.
examples.explanation: According to the rule of parallelism, 'not only' and 'but also' must immediately precede the items being compared (English and French).

sections.title: Exam Strategies and Exceptions
sections.description: Targeted strategies for solving Error Spotting and Cloze Test questions effectively.

strategies.title: Check the Verb Type
strategies.detail: Determine if the verb is transitive or intransitive. Transitive verbs take direct objects without needing a preposition in between.

strategies.title: Verify Conjunction Pairs
strategies.detail: Always check if pair conjunctions are correctly matched. If you see 'No sooner', look for 'than'. If you see 'Hardly/Scarcely', look for 'when'. Mismatched pairs are extremely common exam errors.

exceptions.explanation: Transitive verbs such as Discuss, Describe, Reach, Order, Attack, and Resemble do not take a preposition when used in the Active Voice.
exceptions.example: He ordered for a cup of coffee (Incorrect) -> He ordered a cup of coffee (Correct).
